context.title: The Stages of the Journey
context.summary: A list of the places Israel camped from Rameses in Egypt to the plains of Moab, followed by a command to drive out the land's inhabitants and destroy their idols and shrines.
context.background: Moses is said to have written down these stages (v. 2). Many of the sites are unidentified today. Aaron's death is dated precisely: on Mount Hor, in the fortieth year, fifth month, first day, aged 123 (vv. 38–39).

customs.note: Hilltop shrines for idol worship, a lasting snare in Israel's later history.

watchFor: The list is the whole journey at a glance, Egypt to the Jordan.
Warning: those left in the land will be 'pricks in your eyes, and thorns in your sides' (v. 55).
God's own warning ends the chapter (v. 56).

w: and you will take possession of

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Moses
people.summary: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The fourth son of Ham (Gen. 10:6). His descendants were under a curse in consequence of the transgression of his father (9:22-27). His eldest son, Zidon, was the father of the Sidonians and Phoenicians.

people.name: Arad
people.summary: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Rameses
places.summary: “the land of” (Gen. 47:11), was probably “the land of Goshen” 45:10.

places.name: Succoth
places.summary: The first encampment of the Israelites after leaving Ramesses (Ex. 12:37); the civil name of Pithom.

places.name: Etham
places.summary: Perhaps another name for Khetam, or “fortress,” on the Shur or great wall of Egypt, which extended from the Mediterranean to the Gulf of Suez.

places.name: Baal-zephon
places.summary: Baal of the north, an Egyptian town on the shores of the Gulf of Suez (Ex. 14:2; Num. 33:7), over against which the children of Israel encamped before they crossed the Red Sea.

places.name: Migdol
places.summary: A strongly-fortified place 12 miles from Pelusium, in the north of Egypt (Jer. 44:1; 46:14).

places.name: Pi-hahiroth
places.summary: Place where the reeds grow (LXX. and Copt. read “farmstead”), the name of a place in Egypt where the children of Israel encamped (Ex. 14:2, 9), how long is uncertain.

places.name: Hahiroth
places.summary: from tyndale

places.name: Marah
places.summary: Bitterness, a fountain at the sixth station of the Israelites (Ex. 15:23, 24; Num. 33:8) whose waters were so bitter that they could not drink them.

places.name: Elim
places.summary: Trees, (Ex. 15:27; Num. 33:9), the name of the second station where the Israelites encamped after crossing the Red Sea. It had “twelve wells of water and threescore and ten palm trees.”

places.name: Red sea
places.summary: The sea so called extends along the west coast of Arabia for about 1,400 miles, and separates Asia from Africa. It is connected with the Indian Ocean, of which it is an arm, by the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb.

places.name: Sin
places.summary: Lying between Elim and sinai (Ex. 16:1; comp. Num. 33:11, 12). This was probably the narrow plain of el-Markha, which stretches along the eastern shore of the Red Sea for several miles toward the promontory of Ras Mohammed, the southern extremity of the Sinitic Peninsula.

places.name: Dophkah
places.summary: Knocking, an encampment of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:12).

places.name: Alush
places.summary: One of the places, the last before Rephidim, at which the Hebrews rested on their way to Sinai (Num. 33:13, 14).

places.name: Rephidim
places.summary: Supports, one of the stations of the Israelites, situated in the Wady Feiran, near its junction with the Wady esh-Sheikh. Here no water could be found for the people to drink, and in their impatience they were ready to stone Moses, as if he were the cause of their distress.

places.name: Sinai
places.summary: Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus.

places.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
places.summary: The graves of the longing or of lust, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness.

places.name: Hazeroth
places.summary: Fenced enclosures consisting of “a low wall of stones in which thick bundles of thorny acacia are inserted, the tangled branches and long needle-like spikes forming a perfectly impenetrable hedge around the encampment” of tents and cattle which they sheltered.

places.name: Rithmah
places.summary: Wild broom, a station in the wilderness (Num. 33:18, 19), the “broom valley,” or “valley of broombushes,” the place apparently of the original encampment of Israel, near Kadesh.

places.name: Libnah
places.summary: One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:20, 21).

places.name: Rissah
places.summary: Heap of ruins; dew, a station of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:21, 22).

places.name: Kehelathah
places.summary: Assembly, one of the stations of the Israelites in the desert (Num. 33:22, 23).

places.name: mount Shapher
places.summary: Brightness, one of the stations where Israel encamped in the wilderness (Num. 33:23, 24).

places.name: Haradah
places.summary: Fright; fear, the twenty-fifth station of the Israelites in their wanderings (Num. 33:24).

places.name: Makheloth
places.summary: Assemblies, a station of the Israelites in the desert (Num. 33:25, 26).

places.name: Terah
places.summary: Stopping; station, an encampment of the Hebrews in the wilderness (Num. 33:27, 28).

places.name: Mithkah
places.summary: Sweetness, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:28, 29).

places.name: Hashmonah
places.summary: Fatness, the thirtieth halting-place of the Israelites during their wanderings in the wilderness, not far from Mount Hor (Num. 33:29, 30).

places.name: Moseroth
places.summary: Bonds, one of the stations in the wilderness (Num. 33:30, 31), probably the same as Mosera.

places.name: Bene-jaakan
places.summary: Children of Jaakan (Num. 33:31, 32), the same as Beeroth.

places.name: Abronah
places.summary: R.V., one of Israel’s halting-places in the desert (Num. 33:34, 35), just before Ezion-gaber.

places.name: Ezion-geber
places.summary: The giant’s backbone (so called from the head of a mountain which runs out into the sea), an ancient city and harbour at the north-east end of the Elanitic branch of the Red Sea, the Gulf of Akabah, near Elath or Eloth (Num. 33:35; Deut. 2:8).

places.name: Kadesh
places.summary: Holy, or Kadesh-Barnea, sacred desert of wandering, a place on the south-eastern border of Palestine, about 165 miles from Horeb. It lay in the “wilderness” or “desert of Zin” (Gen. 14:7; Num. 13:3-26; 14:29-33; 20:1; 27:14), on the border of Edom (20:16).

places.name: Zin
places.summary: A low palm-tree, the south-eastern corner of the desert et-Tih, the wilderness of Paran, between the Gulf of Akabah and the head of the Wady Guraiyeh (Num. 13:21).

places.name: Edom
places.summary: Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). “The field of Edom” (Gen. 32:3), “the land of Edom” (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).

places.name: mount Hor
places.summary: One of the mountains of the chain of Seir or Edom, on the confines of Idumea (Num. 20:22-29; 33:37). It was one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (33:37), which they reached in the circuitous route they were obliged to take because the Edomites refused them a passage through their territory.

places.name: Arad
places.summary: Now Tell Arad, a Canaanite city, about 20 miles south of Hebron. The king of Arad “fought against Israel and took of them prisoners” when they were retreating from the confines of Edom (Num. 21:1; 33:40; Judg. 1:16).

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: The country which derived its name from the preceding. The name as first used by the Phoenicians denoted only the maritime plain on which Sidon was built.

places.name: Negeb
places.summary: Heb. Negeb, that arid district to the south of Palestine through which lay the caravan route from Central Palestine to Egypt (Gen. 12:9; 13:1, 3; 46:1-6).

places.name: Zalmonah
places.summary: Shady, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:41, 42).

places.name: Oboth
places.summary: Bottles, an encampment of the Israelites during the wanderings in the wilderness (Num. 33:43), the first after the setting up of the brazen serpent.

places.name: Moab
places.summary: The land of Moab (Jer. 48:24), called also the “country of Moab” (Ruth 1:2, 6; 2:6), on the east of Jordan and the Dead Sea, and south of the Arnon (Num. 21:13, 26).

places.name: Iyim
places.summary: One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:45).

places.name: Almon-diblathaim
places.summary: Two cakes, a city of Moab, on the east of the Dead Sea (Num. 33:46; Jer. 48:22).

places.name: Abarim
places.summary: Regions beyond; i.e., on the east of Jordan, a mountain, or rather a mountain-chain, over against Jericho, to the east and south-east of the Dead Sea, in the land of Moab.

places.name: Nebo
places.summary: A Chaldean god whose worship was introduced into Assyria by Pul (Isa. 46:1; Jer. 48:1). To this idol was dedicated the great temple whose ruins are still seen at Birs Nimrud.

places.name: Jericho
places.summary: Place of fragrance, a fenced city in the midst of a vast grove of palm trees, in the plain of Jordan, over against the place where that river was crossed by the Israelites (Josh. 3:16).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Abel-shittim
places.summary: Meadow of the acacias, frequently called simply “Shittim” (Num. 25:1; Josh. 2:1; Micah 6:5), a place on the east of Jordan, in the plain of Moab, nearly opposite Jericho.

places.name: Beth-jeshimoth
places.summary: House of wastes, or deserts, a town near Abel-shittim, east of Jordan, in the desert of Moab, where the Israelites encamped not long before crossing the Jordan (Num. 33:49; A.V., “Bethjesimoth”).
